title: Shortest reset words of the quadratic automaton modulo p
statement: For a prime p let Q_p be the automaton with states 0, 1, ..., p-1 and two letters, a: x -> x + 1 and b: x -> x^2 (mod p). A reset word is a word that sends every state to one and the same state; let r(p) be the length of a shortest reset word. Determine r(p). The headline cell is p = 101, where 25 <= r(101) <= 31: find a reset word of length at most 30, or prove that 31 is optimal.
submission: Text file: a word over the letters a and b (whitespace and lines starting with # are ignored), applied letter by letter from the left.
score: the length of the word (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: a reset word of length 31 found by beam search over subsets (tools/src/syncbeam.c, beam width 50,000)

context: The Cerny conjecture says that an n-state synchronizing automaton has a reset word of length at most (n-1)^2; it is open in general and proved for several classes, among them circular automata, where one letter permutes the states in a single cycle (Dubuc, RAIRO Theor. Inform. Appl. 32 (1998) 21-34). Q_p is circular (the letter a), so r(p) <= (p-1)^2, but its second letter is the squaring map, whose functional graph modulo p carries the arithmetic of quadratic residues; the exact values below are tiny by comparison (r(101) <= 31 against the bound 10,000) and depend on p in an irregular way (r(17) = 8 and r(97) = 14, while r(47) = 28), so the problem asks how arithmetic controls synchronization. No formula, bound or table for r(p) was found.
references: J. Cerny, Poznamka k homogennym experimentom s konecnymi automatmi, Matematicko-fyzikalny casopis 14 (1964) 208-216
L. Dubuc, Sur les automates circulaires et la conjecture de Cerny, RAIRO Theoretical Informatics and Applications 32 (1998) 21-34

novelty.verdict: new. The automaton x -> x + 1, x -> x^2 (mod p) and its reset thresholds appear in no paper, table or OEIS entry found; the sequence r(3), r(5), ..., r(53) is not in the OEIS.
closest: Dubuc (1998): circular automata satisfy the Cerny bound. That bound applies to Q_p but is far from the values here.

first_values.note: Exact values: breadth-first search over the subsets of states reached from the full set (tools/src/syncq.c); where that search exceeded 14 million subsets, the depth it completed is a lower bound and our beam search gives the upper bound.

baseline.text: 31 for p = 101, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the word in `refs/sync-quadratic.txt`. Lower bound 25: the breadth-first search finished every word of length at most 24 without reaching a single state (tools/src/syncq.c).

bound.source: exhaustive breadth-first search over all subsets reachable by words of length <= 24
